motion: What best explains apparent cosmic purpose: an omnipotent God or a nontraditional purposeful cosmos?

bridges.statement: Show that an omnipotent God better explains apparent cosmic purpose than nontraditional purposive alternatives.
Explain laws, life-permitting order, consciousness, and agency through divine design.
Reconcile divine goodness and power with suffering through justified authority, necessary goods, compensation, responsibility, and character formation.
Show that multiverse proposals relocate rather than discharge fine-tuning.
Defend the omnipotent-God hypothesis as simpler and more unified than limited purposive mechanisms.
Show that cosmic purpose is supported without entailing an omnipotent God and is better explained by a nontraditional purposeful cosmos.
Establish life-permitting fine-tuning as evidence of goal-directedness.
Show that purposeless selection leaves conscious experience unexplained.
Use apparently gratuitous suffering and available moral evidence against an omnipotent perfectly good creator.
Deny that creator-benefaction grants a right to impose suffering.
Reject the multiverse as an adequate inference from the observed universe.
Develop nontraditional purposeful explanations and compare empirical fit with simplicity.
